hook: A monochrome, grainy still image captured by a U.S. military sensor system showing a small dark circular object positioned just right of a central crosshair reticle, with an indistinct mountain range in the background — submitted by the FBI to AARO as an unresolved UAP sighting over the Western United States.
why_it_matters: This image represents a formal military-to-intelligence-agency UAP reporting chain: a U.S. military sensor system captured the object, the FBI submitted it to AARO, and the operator on record was unable to identify it. The manifest explicitly notes the original imagery was redacted before submission, meaning the version available to the public is already sanitized. The incorrect system timestamp undermines precise chronological placement, a recurring metadata reliability issue in PURSUE-release imagery.
key_findings: The image originated from a U.S. military sensor system and was passed to the FBI before submission to AARO — indicating an inter-agency reporting pathway rather than a civilian or commercial source.
The operator who captured the imagery reported being unable to positively identify the UAP, making this an unresolved case by the submitting party's own assessment.
The original imagery was altered with redactions prior to AARO submission; no accompanying mission report was provided, leaving sensor type, altitude, and operational context unknown.
The embedded date/timestamp in the image is acknowledged as incorrect due to the system clock not being set, removing reliable temporal data from the record.

The object appears as a small, dark, circular shape in the upper-right quadrant relative to the reticle center, against a mountain-range background consistent with the listed location of the Western United States.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: AARO is explicitly named as the receiving office for this FBI-submitted military UAP image, placing it squarely within AARO's active collection and reporting mandate.

The use of a military sensor system to capture UAP imagery and route it through official channels echoes the historical role Wright-Patterson played in collecting and archiving aerial anomaly photographs, though no direct institutional link is stated in this document.
